title: Professor Robichaux, A. J. Piron and the competing dance spots
summary: He recalls the left-handed violinist Robichaux, Piron's orchestra at Tranchina's, and the rival spots such as the halfway house.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well he was the one with the music of Panama that I recorded. It was written as a Spanish tune. You play it. And we go boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, you know, and you'll put the old swing to it. Yeah. He says I'll let it to you but to no one else. Then there was AJ P. Rohn. You heard of him?

He had the orchestra at Tranchinas, which was competitive to mine, and also the halfway house. There was Tranchinas, the halfway house where the Brunus boys played, and Carl's. And we've got all the business. So there's a lot of people that are traditionals here in New Orleans that I never heard play. I offered a reward to hear a certain, anybody could ever find, find anybody that heard a certain trumpet player but never did find him. But still he's supposed to be great. Where did he play? Where was I when he was playing? Not that I didn't care. I played my way. Like the motorist called me Connie. Why does he care? Huh?
